For fixed \(i\), the update minimizes \(f(z)=\frac12 z^T A z\) subject to \(z_i=x_i\). For a positive definite quadratic,

\[
\min_{z_i=x_i}\frac12z^TAz
=\frac{x_i^2}{2(A^{-1})_{ii}}.
\]

Here

\[
A^{-1}=\frac1{17}
\begin{bmatrix}
5&-1&-2\\
-1&7&-3\\
-2&-3&11
\end{bmatrix},
\]

so

\[
(A^{-1})_{11}=\frac5{17},\qquad
(A^{-1})_{22}=\frac7{17},\qquad
(A^{-1})_{33}=\frac{11}{17}.
\]

Thus

\[
\mathbb E[f(x^+)\mid x]
=\frac12\left(\frac{17p_1}{5}x_1^2+\frac{17p_2}{7}x_2^2+\frac{17p_3}{11}x_3^2\right).
\]

So \(\rho(p)\) is the largest generalized eigenvalue of

\[
D=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{17p_1}{5},\frac{17p_2}{7},\frac{17p_3}{11}\right)
\]

relative to \(A\). Equivalently, \(\rho(p)\le t\) iff

\[
D\preceq tA.
\]

Write \(D=t\operatorname{diag}(y_1,y_2,y_3)\). Since \(p_1+p_2+p_3=1\),

\[
t(5y_1+7y_2+11y_3)=17.
\]

So minimizing \(t\) means maximizing \(5y_1+7y_2+11y_3\) subject to

\[
A-\operatorname{diag}(y)\succeq0.
\]

Let \(s_1=4-y_1,\ s_2=3-y_2,\ s_3=2-y_3\). Then

\[
A-\operatorname{diag}(y)=
\begin{bmatrix}
s_1&1&1\\
1&s_2&1\\
1&1&s_3
\end{bmatrix}.
\]

We need minimize

\[
5s_1+7s_2+11s_3.
\]

For any positive semidefinite such matrix, using the positive semidefinite Laplacian

\[
Z=
\begin{bmatrix}
5&-\frac12&-\frac92\\
-\frac12&7&-\frac{13}{2}\\
-\frac92&-\frac{13}{2}&11
\end{bmatrix}
\succeq0,
\]

we get

\[
0\le \operatorname{tr}(ZM)
=5s_1+7s_2+11s_3-23.
\]

Hence

\[
5s_1+7s_2+11s_3\ge 23.
\]

Equality occurs at \(s_1=s_2=s_3=1\), giving

\[
y_1=3,\qquad y_2=2,\qquad y_3=1.
\]

Therefore

\[
5y_1+7y_2+11y_3=15+14+11=40,
\]

so

\[
\rho_*=\frac{17}{40}.
\]

Finally,

\[
p_i=(A^{-1})_{ii}\rho_* y_i,
\]

hence

\[
p_1:p_2:p_3
=
5\cdot3:7\cdot2:11\cdot1
=
15:14:11.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(\rho_*,p_1:p_2:p_3\right)=\left(\frac{17}{40},\,15:14:11\right)}.
\]
